newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 16.09 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 16.09 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 206 basis points to 16.09 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 60 billion bolivars of 178- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 18.16 percent coupon for a price of 100.95 percent. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 18.16 percent

The bank also sold 20 billion bolivars of 267-day notes with a 18.56 percent coupon at 100.75 percent and 20 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 18.98 percent coupon at an average price of 100.56 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 203 basis points to 17.42 percent for the 267-day bills and 211 basis points to 18.32 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
